analysis:
Examined all supplied documentation excerpts, release-file metadata and bounded patches against the indexed threat model and detailed T-041. The substantive visible change is release routing: docs/developer/test.md:1048-1059 describes push-to-dev invocation of the reusable release workflow with inherited secrets and Developer ID signing, replacing the former dispatch-only lane without signing authority. Lines 1066-1078 describe staging-only master publication, dev ancestry gates and final-app requirement checks. The provider-release.md patch at head lines 12-28 likewise separates master/staging, tags/production and dev-branch releases. These are documented contracts, not evidence that workflow enforcement succeeds or fails; no independently supported regression can be reported from this batch.
Surrounding documentation preserves distinctions between synthetic tests and native qualification, isolated encrypted cache testing and account refusal (test.md:604-619, 708-722), App Attest authorization and exact-artifact evidence (849-885), and content-free telemetry (1289-1298). No visible change weakens those contracts or T-041's cache isolation/encryption controls.
Integration should verify the actual release-dev-branch.yml/release-provider.yml routing, secret guards, dev ancestry checks and publication/registration separation, especially whether newly signed dev artifacts can acquire production release or serving authority (A-005, A-011, A-017, T-013, T-054) or alter fan-helper trust (TB-010, T-045). Inherited secrets alone do not establish exposure. provider-release.md has only metadata and a truncated patch here; its other changed ranges remain unexamined source. The uncertainty is material because the documentation describes newly available signing authority, while executable controls and most of the release runbook are outside this batch.
